paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of in-situ nitride-reinforced refractory high-entropy alloy TiZrHfNbTa matrix composites

Fig. 1 depicts the XRD pattern of the as-cast composites N0.1~N0.4, and a single BCC phase is identified in all the composites, which corresponds to the TiZrHfNbTa matrix.
With the introduction of nitrogen, the traces of peaks in accordance with FCC MN-type (M and N refer to the metallic and nitrogen element, respectively) nitrides appear
With the increase of nitrogen content, the nitrides grow up obviously and change from sphere-like to needle-like.

STEM bright field (BF) image shows that the needle-like nitrides (dark phase) are distributed in the matrix (bright phase). The corresponding EDX mapping results show that Zr, Hf and N are enriched in the needle-like nitrides
Fig. 3 (b) shows dislocations within the BCC matrix and several stacking faults within the precipitates, which would be formed during the fast solidification process.

The significant improvement of yield strength in this study can be attributed to the load transfer effect (σLT), dislocation strengthening (σDis), and Orowan mechanism (σOro)
The significant improvement of yield strength in this study can be attributed to the load transfer effect (σLT), dislocation strengthening (σDis), and Orowan mechanism (σOro)

When the N content is low (N0.1), the MN nitrides are only able to grow into the fine particles and herein the nitrides act as obstacles to dislocation movements rather than the second phase to withstand the load transferred from the matrix, so in N0.1 the Orowan mechanism dominates.
As illustrated in Fig. 5, σLT contributes more to the total improvement, indicating that in N0.4 the nitrides act more as a load-bearing phase rather than obstacles for dislocation movement.
